items.title: 'Will definitely assist with everyday costs': Award workers welcome wage rise
items.description: Australia's minimum wage will increase by 5.97 per cent, and minimum award workers will get a 4.75 per cent pay boost, in the Fair Work Commission's (FWC) annual wage review.

items.title: Trump's reportedly 'crazy' phone call to Netanyahu reminds world who calls the shots
items.description: Donald Trump's intervention in Benjamin Netanyahu's plans to strike Beirut goes to the heart of the relationship between the two sides, in that support may be limited, particularly if it threatens what the US president really wants.

items.title: NSW Police signals body-worn cameras change after Four Corners investigation
items.description: NSW Police will move to the mandatory use of body-worn cameras for sworn officers in the wake of allegations of a culture of impunity within the police force.

items.description: Moscow targeted Kyiv and other cities, killing multiple people, damaging buildings and leaving wounded trapped under rubble, local authorities say.

items.title: Plan for Stars and Renegades to merge in BBL shake-up
items.description: Cricket Victoria plans to merge the Stars and Renegades into one 'Melbourne' team.

items.title: 'It is very scary': Parents shocked school was target of alleged deadly plot
items.description: A 13-year-old boy has been charged with violent extremist offences and posed an "imminent threat" to the school.

items.title: Prominent surgeon Dr Reza Adib suspended by health ombudsman
items.description: Obesity surgeon Reza Adib has been suspended from practising medicine as he faces rape charges.

items.title: Two men believed trapped in cave for nearly two weeks as rescue mission turns to vertical tunnels

items.title: 'Terribly sad day': Beer experts say Boag's closure points to growing cost of brewing

items.title: What the polls reveal about One Nation's growing appeal

items.title: Why the 'dig of the century' is happening underneath Notre Dame
items.description: More than a year after France's famed Notre Dame reopened, an archaeological exploration going thousands of years into the history of Paris has begun just metres below the cathedral's ground floor.

items.title: Councillor defends calling CEO 'despicable, disgusting woman'
items.description: A regional councillor has justified using offensive language towards the council's CEO in multiple emails and social media videos, claiming that he was attacked first and that "it’s a two-way street".

items.title: Copper thieves are more brazen and taking exceptional risks, demolition experts say

items.title: Owning a dog was nothing like I'd imagined
items.description: I completely neglected to give much thought to whether my personality would slot into a dog's lifestyle. Spoiler — it did not.

items.title: Search for Tasmanian devil 'Mary' missing from popular Gold Coast wildlife park
items.description: The recently arrived young devil has been kept in a secure indoor facility while quarantining, but was noticed missing on Tuesday morning.

items.title: Why make-up sex may not be fixing anything

items.description: South Australia's One Nation has vowed to block every Labor government bill following a dispute over staffing allocations.

items.title: Katter attempt to dodge ban and debate abortion access shot down by Qld government
items.description: The subject became an issue ahead of the last Queensland election in October 2024, with premier David Crisafulli implementing a ban on abortion debate after winning government.

items.title: Minimum rental standards
items.description: Think your rental falls below the minimum standards?  In a rental crisis, people are taking what they can get and it doesn't always match the listed description.  The rules may vary across Australia but renters can take the issue to a tribunal such as NCAT or VCAT.  It's where you'd go to force repairs, seek compensation or even push for a lower rent.

items.title: Man charged over weekend double stabbing across Melbourne
items.description: The 27-year-old is accused of two separate stabbings on the opposite sides of Melbourne.

items.title: ICAC to probe allegations against University of Wollongong executives
items.description: The anti-corruption commission is to examine allegations about recruitment and the employment of a consultancy firm against Chancellor Michael Still and other members of the university's executive.
